name: QA graph census
description: QA only (coverage evidence, docs/design/breadth.md §3): observes the most recent Codex threads so their history loads, then writes <dataDir>/files/census.json: for every type the native provider put, how many instances there are and how many have each state field and link. Written at activation and whenever <dataDir>/files/run exists (the file is removed). When <dataDir>/files/approve or deny exists (removed), it approves once or denies the newest pending native approval and logs the outcome to files/act.log. When files/project-rename, project-remove or project-reveal exists (removed), it runs that operation on the LocalProject the file names ({"id", "name"?}) and logs the outcome to files/act.log; the projects' named events go to files/events.log. Files file-open, file-reveal and folder-reveal ({"path"}) run that operation on the File or Folder; observe-folder ({"path"}) observes a folder's files from then on and writes what it lists to files/folder.json; File events go to files/events.log too. approve-always approves the newest pending native approval 'always' (the user is asked first). app-open ({"id", "path", "kind"?}), app-set-computer-use ({"id", "level"}) and list-apps (writes files/apps.json) act on ExternalApp; its events go to files/events.log. git ({"projectId", "op": createBranch | switchBranch | branch, "name"}) acts on the project's GitRepository and logs its state; Repository and Environment events go to files/events.log. instructions-edit ({"path", "text"}) and instructions-open ({"path"}) act on the Instructions at that path, list-instructions writes files/instructions.json; Instructions events go to files/events.log. action-run ({"id", "thread"?}) runs a ProjectAction; list-actions writes files/actions.json; Command events go to files/events.log. invoke ({"type", "id", "op", "args"?}) runs any granted operation on a native instance and logs it to files/act.log. list ({"type", "where"?}) writes files/list.json with that type's native instances a where keeps (state, links and the attached values it may see). The D6-D9 operations (commands, automations, notifications, changes, history, review, comments, pull requests, terminals, the browser and computer use) are granted for invoke. related ({"ref", "relation"}) writes files/related.json with the instance's relation (a thread's presentations, a Window's children). presentations-on and presentations-off start and stop logging the Presentation instances' named events to files/events.log (systems.md S10). ui-read ({"type"?, "window"?, "subject"?}) writes files/ui-read.json through ctx.ui.read; ui-act ({"ref", "op", "args"?}) runs a presentation's operation through ctx.ui.act and logs it to files/act.log (E7). rule ({"op": hide | decorate | default | order | reorder | update | remove, "id", "presentation"?, ...}) puts, changes or takes away one of its UI rules, defaults (ctx.graph.defaults) or sidebar orders (ctx.ui.sidebar.order) while the app is idle and logs the outcome to files/act.log (layouts D3). It gives the agent (graph-integrity G3.5, the SDK's helpers on the agent's inputs) a tool qa_echo, the skill qa-census-skill (skills/) and instructions: a chat's (the QA codeword) and each turn's (the QA fruit).
